steps: 1. A trapezoid is a four-sided shape with one pair of parallel bases
2. Add the two bases together: (b1 + b2)
3. Multiply by the perpendicular height, then take half

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Budgets
revealWordProblem.text:
The parking lot shown is being repaved. Asphalt for the parking lot costs $3.95 per square foot, and labor costs about $3 per square foot.
Question: What total budget do you recommend for repaving the parking lot? Show how you found the area.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A diagram of a parking lot made of a rectangle and a trapezoid, labeled 25 feet, 70 feet, 57 feet, 40 feet, and 54 feet.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Decompose the lot by splitting along the horizontal line at the top of the 40-foot section. The upper rectangle is 25 feet wide and 70 − 40 = 30 feet tall, so its area is 25 × 30 = 750 square feet. The lower trapezoid has parallel bases 25 + 57 = 82 feet and 54 feet, and height 40 feet. Its area is ½ × (82 + 54) × 40 = 2,720 square feet. Total area = 750 + 2,720 = 3,470 square feet. Asphalt and labor together cost about $3.95 + $3.00 = $6.95 per square foot, giving 3,470 × $6.95 = $24,116.50. A budget of about $24,200 covers this estimate; any extra contingency should be stated separately.

questions.stem: What is the area of a trapezoid with bases 6 cm and 10 cm, and height 4 cm?
choiceFeedback: 24 is 6 × 4 — only one base was used. Add both bases first: 6 + 10 = 16.
40 is 10 × 4 — only the longer base. A trapezoid uses the average of BOTH bases.
64 is (6 + 10) × 4 without the ÷ 2. Take half of the bases' sum before multiplying by the height.
hints: A trapezoid has two bases (6 cm and 10 cm) plus a height (4 cm) — all three belong in the formula.
Use A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h: add the bases first, then multiply by the height, then take half.
Add 6 + 10 to get the base sum, multiply that by 4, then cut the result in half.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de un trapecio con bases de 6 cm y 10 cm, y altura de 4 cm?
questions.explanationEs: A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h = ½ × (6 + 10) × 4 = ½ × 16 × 4 = 32 cm cuadrados.
hintsEs: Un trapecio tiene dos bases (6 cm y 10 cm) más una altura (4 cm): las tres van en la fórmula.
Usa A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h: suma primero las bases, luego multiplica por la altura y luego saca la mitad.
Suma 6 + 10 para obtener la suma de las bases, multiplica eso por 4 y luego parte el resultado a la mitad.

questions.stem: A trapezoid has an area of 45 sq ft, bases of 7 ft and 11 ft. What is the height?
choiceFeedback: Check it: (7 + 11) ÷ 2 × 3 = 27, not 45. Double the area first: 2 × 45 = 90, then ÷ 18.
Check it: (7 + 11) ÷ 2 × 10 = 90 — that's double the area. Divide 90 by 18, not by 9.
hints: You already know the area (45 sq ft) and both bases (7 ft and 11 ft) — the height is what's missing.
Simplify first: ½ × (7 + 11) = 9. So the equation becomes 45 = 9 × h.
Divide 45 by 9 to find the height in feet.
questions.stemEs: Un trapecio tiene un área de 45 ft cuadrados y bases de 7 ft y 11 ft. ¿Cuál es la altura?
hintsEs: Ya conoces el área (45 pies²) y ambas bases (7 pies y 11 pies): lo que falta es la altura.
Simplifica primero: ½ × (7 + 11) = 9. Así la ecuación se vuelve 45 = 9 × h.
Divide 45 entre 9 para hallar la altura en pies.

questions.stem: What is the first step when finding the area of a trapezoid?
choices: Subtract the shorter base from the longer base
questions.explanation: The formula is A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. The first step is to add the two parallel bases.
choiceFeedback: The two bases get ADDED, not multiplied — they are the parallel lengths the formula averages.
Subtracting tells you how much longer one base is, not the combined length the formula needs.
The divide-by-2 comes later, applied after the bases are combined — the first move gathers both bases.
hints: Look at the trapezoid formula A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Parentheses show what happens first.
Ask what (b₁ + b₂) means: are the two parallel bases combined by adding, multiplying, or subtracting?
Say the formula in words: 'half of (base one ___ base two) times height.' The word that fills the blank is your first step.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el primer paso para hallar el área de un trapecio?
questions.explanationEs: La fórmula es A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. El primer paso es sumar las dos bases paralelas.
choicesEs: Restar la base más corta de la base más larga
hintsEs: Mira la fórmula del trapecio A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Los paréntesis muestran qué se hace primero.
Pregunta qué significa (b₁ + b₂): ¿las dos bases paralelas se combinan sumando, multiplicando o restando?
Di la fórmula en palabras: 'la mitad de (base uno ___ base dos) por la altura'. La palabra que llena el espacio es tu primer paso.

steps: 1. A trapezoid is a four-sided shape with one pair of parallel bases
2. Add the two bases together: (b1 + b2)
3. Multiply by the perpendicular height, then take half
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Area of Trapezoids is forgetting the ½ in A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h. After adding the bases and multiplying by the height, students stop there instead of taking half — for example, with bases 6 ft and 10 ft and a height of 4 ft, they compute (6 + 10) × 4 = 64 sq ft instead of taking half to get the correct 32 sq ft. That unhalved number is really the area of the parallelogram made from two trapezoids, not the area of one trapezoid. Before you submit, always ask: "Did I take half of my last answer?"

level1.stem: A trapezoid has bases of 1 m and 5 m. Its height is 4 m. Find its area.
level1.stemEs: Un trapecio tiene bases de 1 m y 5 m. Su altura mide 4 m. Halla su área.
hints: Add the bases. Multiply by the height. Then take half.
hintsEs: Suma las bases. Multiplica por la altura. Luego toma la mitad.
level1.explanation: Add the two bases: 1 + 5 = 6 Multiply by the height: 6 × 4 = 24 Take half: 1/2 × 24 = 12
level1.explanationEs: Suma las dos bases: 1 + 5 = 6 Multiplica por la altura: 6 × 4 = 24 Toma la mitad: 1/2 × 24 = 12

level1.stem: A trapezoid has bases of 3 ft and 9 ft. Its height is 2 ft. Find its area.
level1.stemEs: Un trapecio tiene bases de 3 pies y 9 pies. Su altura mide 2 pies. Halla su área.
hints: Add 3 + 9 first.
hintsEs: Primero suma 3 + 9.
level1.explanation: Add the two bases: 3 + 9 = 12 Multiply by the height: 12 × 2 = 24 Take half: 1/2 × 24 = 12
level1.explanationEs: Suma las dos bases: 3 + 9 = 12 Multiplica por la altura: 12 × 2 = 24 Toma la mitad: 1/2 × 24 = 12

level1.stem: A garden is a trapezoid. Its parallel sides are 6 m and 8 m. Its height is 5 m. What is its area?
level1.stemEs: Un jardín es un trapecio. Sus lados paralelos miden 6 m y 8 m. Su altura mide 5 m. ¿Cuál es su área?
hints: Add the bases. Multiply by the height. Then take half.
hintsEs: Suma las bases. Multiplica por la altura. Luego toma la mitad.
level1.explanation: Add the two bases: 6 + 8 = 14 Multiply by the height: 14 × 5 = 70 Take half: 1/2 × 70 = 35
level1.explanationEs: Suma las dos bases: 6 + 8 = 14 Multiplica por la altura: 14 × 5 = 70 Toma la mitad: 1/2 × 70 = 35

level1.stem: A trapezoid has bases of 2 in and 4 in. Its height is 3 in. Find its area.
level1.stemEs: Un trapecio tiene bases de 2 pulg y 4 pulg. Su altura mide 3 pulg. Halla su área.
hints: Add the bases. Multiply by the height. Then take half.
hintsEs: Suma las bases. Multiplica por la altura. Luego toma la mitad.
level1.explanation: Add the two bases: 2 + 4 = 6 Multiply by the height: 6 × 3 = 18 Take half: 1/2 × 18 = 9
level1.explanationEs: Suma las dos bases: 2 + 4 = 6 Multiplica por la altura: 6 × 3 = 18 Toma la mitad: 1/2 × 18 = 9

level1.stem: A trapezoid has bases of 12 ft and 8 ft. Its height is 7 ft. Find its area.
level1.stemEs: Un trapecio tiene bases de 12 pies y 8 pies. Su altura mide 7 pies. Halla su área.
hints: Add the bases first. Then multiply by 7 and take half.
hintsEs: Primero suma las bases. Luego multiplica por 7 y toma la mitad.
level1.explanation: Add the two bases: 12 + 8 = 20 Multiply by the height: 20 × 7 = 140 Take half: 1/2 × 140 = 70
level1.explanationEs: Suma las dos bases: 12 + 8 = 20 Multiplica por la altura: 20 × 7 = 140 Toma la mitad: 1/2 × 140 = 70

level2.stem: Rosa finds the area of a trapezoid with bases 7 cm and 3 cm and height 6 cm. She writes 7 × 6 = 42. What is the correct area?
level2.stemEs: Rosa halla el área de un trapecio con bases de 7 cm y 3 cm y altura de 6 cm. Ella escribe 7 × 6 = 42. ¿Cuál es el área correcta?
hints: Rosa used only one base. A trapezoid has two bases.
hintsEs: Rosa usó solo una base. Un trapecio tiene dos bases.
level2.explanation: Add both bases: 7 + 3 = 10 Multiply by the height: 10 × 6 = 60 Take half: 1/2 × 60 = 30
level2.explanationEs: Suma las dos bases: 7 + 3 = 10 Multiplica por la altura: 10 × 6 = 60 Toma la mitad: 1/2 × 60 = 30

level2.stem: A trapezoid has bases of 2.5 m and 5.5 m. Its height is 6 m. Find its area.
level2.stemEs: Un trapecio tiene bases de 2.5 m y 5.5 m. Su altura mide 6 m. Halla su área.
hints: Add the decimal bases first. The sum is a whole number.
hintsEs: Primero suma las bases decimales. La suma es un número entero.
level2.explanation: Add the two bases: 2.5 + 5.5 = 8 Multiply by the height: 8 × 6 = 48 Take half: 1/2 × 48 = 24
level2.explanationEs: Suma las dos bases: 2.5 + 5.5 = 8 Multiplica por la altura: 8 × 6 = 48 Toma la mitad: 1/2 × 48 = 24

level2.stem: A trapezoid has bases of 4 m and 10 m. Its height is 6 m. Find its area.
level2.stemEs: Un trapecio tiene bases de 4 m y 10 m. Su altura mide 6 m. Halla su área.
hints: Add the bases. Multiply by the height. Then take half.
hintsEs: Suma las bases. Multiplica por la altura. Luego toma la mitad.
level2.explanation: Add the two bases: 4 + 10 = 14 Multiply by the height: 14 × 6 = 84 Take half: 1/2 × 84 = 42
level2.explanationEs: Suma las dos bases: 4 + 10 = 14 Multiplica por la altura: 14 × 6 = 84 Toma la mitad: 1/2 × 84 = 42

level2.stem: A trapezoid has an area of 66 square inches. Its height is 6 inches. One base is 8 inches. How long is the other base?
level2.stemEs: Un trapecio tiene un área de 66 pulgadas cuadradas. Su altura mide 6 pulgadas. Una base mide 8 pulgadas. ¿Cuánto mide la otra base?
hints: Double the area. Divide by the height. That gives the sum of both bases.
hintsEs: Duplica el área. Divide entre la altura. Eso da la suma de las dos bases.
level2.explanation: Double the area to undo the half: 66 × 2 = 132 Divide by the height: 132 ÷ 6 = 22 Subtract the base you know: 22 − 8 = 14
level2.explanationEs: Duplica el área para deshacer la mitad: 66 × 2 = 132 Divide entre la altura: 132 ÷ 6 = 22 Resta la base que conoces: 22 − 8 = 14

level2.stem: A road sign is a trapezoid. Its parallel sides are 20 inches and 30 inches. Its height is 16 inches. What is the area of the sign?
level2.stemEs: Una señal de tránsito es un trapecio. Sus lados paralelos miden 20 pulgadas y 30 pulgadas. Su altura mide 16 pulgadas. ¿Cuál es el área de la señal?
hints: The parallel sides are the bases. Add them first.
hintsEs: Los lados paralelos son las bases. Primero súmalos.
level2.explanation: Add the two bases: 20 + 30 = 50 Multiply by the height: 50 × 16 = 800 Take half: 1/2 × 800 = 400
level2.explanationEs: Suma las dos bases: 20 + 30 = 50 Multiplica por la altura: 50 × 16 = 800 Toma la mitad: 1/2 × 800 = 400

level3.stem: A trapezoidal window has parallel edges of 4 feet and 8 feet and a height of 5 feet. What is its area?
choiceFeedback: That adds all three measurements. The rule multiplies the average of the parallel edges by the height.
That is 4 times 5, using only one of the two parallel edges. Average them first.
The halving step was skipped. 4 plus 8, times 5, is twice the area.
level3.explanation: Area = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h = ½ × (4 + 8) × 5 = ½ × 12 × 5 = 30 square feet.

level3.stem: A trapezoid has bases of 6 cm and 14 cm and a height of 5 cm. Jay finds 20 ÷ 2 = 10, then 10 × 5 = 50. Lin finds 6 × 5 + 14 × 5 = 100. Who is right?
level3.stemEs: Un trapecio tiene bases de 6 cm y 14 cm y una altura de 5 cm. Jay calcula 20 ÷ 2 = 10 y luego 10 × 5 = 50. Lin calcula 6 × 5 + 14 × 5 = 100. ¿Quién tiene razón?
hints: Use the formula yourself. Then compare.
hintsEs: Usa tú la fórmula. Luego compara.
level3.explanation: Add the bases and take half: (6 + 14) ÷ 2 = 10 Multiply by the height: 10 × 5 = 50
level3.explanationEs: Suma las bases y toma la mitad: (6 + 14) ÷ 2 = 10 Multiplica por la altura: 10 × 5 = 50
choices: Jay: the area is 50 square centimeters
Lin: the area is 100 square centimeters
choicesEs: Jay: el área es 50 centímetros cuadrados
Lin: el área es 100 centímetros cuadrados
choiceFeedback: Lin found the area of two copies of the trapezoid. She forgot to take half.
50 and 100 are different areas, so both cannot be right.

level3.stem: A trapezoid has an area of 70 square centimeters. Its bases are 6 cm and 8 cm. What is its height?
level3.stemEs: Un trapecio tiene un área de 70 centímetros cuadrados. Sus bases miden 6 cm y 8 cm. ¿Cuál es su altura?
hints: Double the area. Then divide by the sum of the bases.
hintsEs: Duplica el área. Luego divide entre la suma de las bases.
level3.explanation: Double the area to undo the half: 70 × 2 = 140 Divide by the sum of the bases: 6 + 8 = 14; 140 ÷ 14 = 10
level3.explanationEs: Duplica el área para deshacer la mitad: 70 × 2 = 140 Divide entre la suma de las bases: 6 + 8 = 14; 140 ÷ 14 = 10

level3.stem: A patio is a trapezoid with an area of 150 square feet. Its front and back edges are parallel and 10 feet apart. The front edge is 12 feet. How long is the back edge?
level3.stemEs: Un patio es un trapecio con un área de 150 pies cuadrados. Sus bordes de adelante y de atrás son paralelos y están a 10 pies de distancia. El borde de adelante mide 12 pies. ¿Cuánto mide el borde de atrás?
hints: The two edges are the bases. The distance between them is the height.
hintsEs: Los dos bordes son las bases. La distancia entre ellos es la altura.
level3.explanation: Double the area to undo the half: 150 × 2 = 300 Divide by the height: 300 ÷ 10 = 30 Subtract the base you know: 30 − 12 = 18
level3.explanationEs: Duplica el área para deshacer la mitad: 150 × 2 = 300 Divide entre la altura: 300 ÷ 10 = 30 Resta la base que conoces: 30 − 12 = 18

level3.stem: A trapezoid has a height of 4 cm and an area of 30 square centimeters. The long base is 3 cm longer than the short base. How long is the short base?
level3.stemEs: Un trapecio tiene una altura de 4 cm y un área de 30 centímetros cuadrados. La base larga mide 3 cm más que la base corta. ¿Cuánto mide la base corta?
hints: First find the sum of the two bases. Then share it so one base is 3 more.
hintsEs: Primero halla la suma de las dos bases. Luego repártela para que una base sea 3 más.
level3.explanation: Find the sum of the bases: 30 × 2 = 60; 60 ÷ 4 = 15 Take away the extra 3, then split: 15 − 3 = 12; 12 ÷ 2 = 6 Check the two bases: 6 + 9 = 15; 1/2 × 15 × 4 = 30
level3.explanationEs: Halla la suma de las bases: 30 × 2 = 60; 60 ÷ 4 = 15 Quita los 3 de más y luego reparte: 15 − 3 = 12; 12 ÷ 2 = 6 Comprueba las dos bases: 6 + 9 = 15; 1/2 × 15 × 4 = 30
